rationale: Replace the two superseded measurements in the transfer account with the successor receipt's actual readings: the demoted target still saw itself as a voter, yet the voters refused it and the target campaigned for eight samples while about 80 ms had no leader, against zero in the voter control. Both receipts are cited with joint history, and the knowledge records gain the successor's indices.

knowledge.statement: Automatic leadership transfer and explicit leadership transfer use different target checks: pickServer (used when no id is given) skips every server whose Suffrage is not Voter, while an explicit id is only looked up in leaderState.replState, which contains an entry for every configured server including non-voters, and a successful lookup proceeds to replicate and send TimeoutNow without consulting suffrage.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state with a committed latest configuration containing a non-voter; explicit LeadershipTransferToServer(id) for that member.

knowledge.statement: A voter that receives a RequestVote from a candidate absent from its latest configuration rejects it before any term handling, but a candidate that is present yet not a voter is handled later: the voter first adopts a higher term and steps down to follower, and only then rejects the vote because hasVote is false. timeoutNow performs no term, leader or membership check and immediately marks the receiver as a leadership-transfer candidate.
knowledge.conditions: Voter with a known latest configuration; RequestVote with LeadershipTransfer=true from a configured non-voter at a higher term.

interpretations.joint_history: Receipt 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f is the successor of the same fixed experiment lineage under this investigation: identical case names, admissions, assertions and cluster construction, with two added measurements (the target's own configuration view before the transfer, and per-sample candidate/leaderless counts read from each member's State()). The two receipts agree on the decisive outcome of all four comparisons, so their events describe the same subject and can be read together; the successor replaces the earlier receipt only for the two quantities the earlier run left unmeasured.
interpretations.rationale: Conclusion: violated, and the scoped defect is asserted. A leadership transfer that explicitly names a member the configuration marks as a non-voter is admitted, completes its future without error, and does not install that member as leader; the attempt instead forces an election round in which every member's term advances, leadership lands on a member the caller did not name, and leadership is absent for a measurable interval. Evidence, two receipts of the same experiment lineage. Parsed index 1 of receipt d436029b08c5425aa5aec577901cb8ba and of successor receipt 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f, the control where the explicit target is an ordinary voter: target_ever_leader=true, final_leader_is_target=true, future_ok=true, target_term_after=3 with other_member_term_max_after=3, so the mechanism installs the named target with a single term advance. Parsed index 3 of both receipts, the trigger where one non-leader member was demoted with DemoteVoter before the transfer: future_ok=true with an empty future_error, target_ever_leader=false, final_leader_is_target=false, target_term_after=4 and other_member_term_max_after=4, while the case event (parsed index 2) records target_demoted=true and transfer_target_role=nonvoter. The successor adds two measurements that resolve what the first run left open: the demoted target's own GetConfiguration still reported its role as voter before the transfer (so it believed it was eligible and campaigned in good faith), yet the voters rejected it; and the trigger produced 8 candidate samples with 8 leaderless samples (about 80 ms with no member reporting Leader) out of 470 samples at roughly 10 ms spacing, against 0 candidate and 0 leaderless samples out of 471 in the control. The two cases differ only in the target's suffrage, so the outcome difference is attributable to eligibility, not to the transfer path, harness or transport timing. Mechanism from source: leaderLoop resolves an explicit id only through leaderState.replState (raft.go:687-742), which startStopReplication populates for every configured server including non-voters, whereas the automatic path's pickServer skips non-voters outright (raft.go:2186-2206); leadershipTransfer replicates the target and sends TimeoutNow (raft.go:991-1023), and timeoutNow (raft.go:2232-2237) marks the receiver as a leadership-transfer candidate with no suffrage, term, leader or membership check; electSelf raises the target's term and asks every voter, whose requestVote handler adopts the higher term and steps down before rejecting the non-voter (raft.go:1696-1707). The trigger's term pattern (target and all other members at 4, one step beyond the rejected round) and its leaderless interval match exactly that path, while the control's single-step advance to 3 matches a successful transfer. Consequence under the exercised conditions: a caller that names a serving but non-voting member receives a completed transfer with no error, no transfer of authority, an extra election round that raises every member's term, and a leaderless interval whose length follows the configured election timeout.
counterevidence: The documentation's promise is soft rather than a guarantee: it says it is 'very likely' the target wins and that a follower which cannot be promoted 'will fail gracefully' (api.go:1296-1330), and the leaderLoop code deliberately reports nil with the message 'lost leadership during transfer (expected)', which can be read as the future reporting only that leadership was relinquished. The claim therefore rests on the admission of an ineligible target and on the observed outcome, not on the future's wording alone.
The control case shows the same mechanism transfers leadership correctly to a voter, so the defect is specific to the eligibility of an explicitly named target, not to leadership transfer in general.

The measured disruption is small in absolute terms because the cluster ran with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms): 8 samples and about 80 ms without a leader, one extra election round. The interval follows the configured election timeout, so a production configuration of about 1 s would scale it accordingly; the 80 ms figure is not a bound for other settings.

No committed entry was lost, no vote was counted for an ineligible candidate, and no decision-safety property was contradicted in either case; what is contradicted is the completion signal and the authority outcome of the explicit transfer.
limitations: Both runs exercised one cluster size (four members, three voters after the demotion) and one relationship: a leader transferring to a non-leader member. Transfer initiated while the leader later regains leadership, and clusters whose only non-voter is the sole reachable member, were not tested.

Leaderless counts are sampled every ~10 ms over roughly 4.7 s of the 5 s window (470 samples); a gap shorter than the sample spacing would be missed, so 80 ms is a lower bound for the trigger and the control's zero does not prove uninterrupted leadership.

The demoted target's own configuration still showed it as a voter at transfer time in both runs. The exercised case is therefore a member that believes it is eligible while the voters' committed view refuses it; a target that already knows it is a non-voter was not exercised, although timeoutNow's unconditional candidacy implies it would campaign as well.
That the voter members had committed the demotion before the transfer is inferred from their rejection and term adoption, not from reading each voter's configuration.

Out of scope: whether an unprivileged or misconfigured peer could send TimeoutNow directly, even though timeoutNow performs no term, leader or membership check (raft.go:2232-2237); that path was not exercised here.

knowledge.assertion: An explicit transfer target is resolved only through leaderState.replState, which includes non-voters, while pickServer skips non-voters.
A voter adopts a higher term and steps down before rejecting a configured non-voter candidate, and timeoutNow forces candidacy without checking suffrage or term.
